The first 50 orders receive complimentary personalization and expedited shipping.

Why: the headline, the reason to join and the email field all sit above the fold. The First 50 line adds urgency without a discount.
How to build: Klaviyo embedded form inside a Broadcast section. A hidden field saves the signup source (landing, homepage banner, announcement bar, menu) on each profile.
Why: the visitor sees at once that it worked and what happens next, so they don't sign up twice or wonder where the link is.
How to build: the Klaviyo form's success message replaces the form in place. No new page, so there is nothing extra to build or track.
Needs your OK: the hero image. This is a mood image of the four shades; the final one comes from the new collection's photography and never shows a full product before Nov 23.

How to build: products are Unlisted (no search, collections or menu). An automatic discount takes 100% off the hidden Personalization product and a $0 expedited rate applies, both switched off by Shopify Flow at order 50.
Policy: one First 50 benefit per customer; repeat orders are tagged First50-repeat for review because Shopify can't block guest repeats at checkout.

F · Existing popup and welcome flow

Nov 20–26

The store's signup popup is hidden on the waitlist page and the new product pages, so visitors see one form, not two. Waitlist signups are filtered out of the store's regular welcome flow, so they never get its discount on a launch built on "value, not discounts".

The six launch emails

One welcome flow and five campaigns in Klaviyo, built in the store's fonts and colours. Product cards show no colour variants; colours are chosen on the product page. Emails 1, 2, 3 and 5 carry a live countdown.

How the emails flow

Nov 20–27
How to build: Klaviyo has no built-in countdown, so each timer is a live GIF from a countdown tool (for example Sendtric) added as an image block. It shows the right time whenever the email is opened.
Why: buyers leave the reminder segment the moment they order, so nobody who has bought gets "ends tonight".

How it all connects

Every channel sends people to one page. Every person on the list gets one clear next step on each date, and buyers drop out of the reminders as soon as they order.

What we will track

Targets to agree with the client
WhatWhere we see itWhy it matters
Waitlist page visitors and signup rateShopify Analytics, GA4 through GTMShows whether the page converts; the first number to fix if signups are low
Waitlist signups, by sourceKlaviyo, profile property signup_sourceWhich touchpoint fills the list: banner, bar, menu, email or social
Opens and clicks for each emailKlaviyoInterest before Nov 24; low clicks on Email 3 is an early warning
Private Access orders and revenueShopify, orders tagged Pre-order, Nov 24–26The main result of the launch
First 50 countShopify Flow counterSwitches the offer off at 50 and changes the announcement bar
Personalization take-rateShopify, orders tagged PersonalizedWhether people pay for initials once it's no longer free
Repeat First 50 attemptsShopify, tag First50-repeatOrders the team reviews by hand
Revenue from Email 5Klaviyo attributed revenueHow much the last-chance reminder recovers
Waitlist to buyer conversionKlaviyo segment "Waitlist – No purchase yet"Share of the list that bought during Private Access
Launch-week sales of the new collectionShopify, by product and variantWhich pieces and shades sell; guides reorders
